**CmdRunAction + CmdOutputObservation (multiple)**
THOUGHT: Analyzed `opt_init`, `opt_cleanup`, `opt_error`, `propedom`, `find_edom`, `opt_root`, `gen_cmp`, `gen_ncmp`, `new_block`, `newchunk` functions. Confirmed the double-free mechanism: when `opt_init` fails partway through allocations, it frees already-allocated pointers then calls `opt_error` which longjmps to `bpf_optimize`, which calls `opt_cleanup` freeing the same pointers again. Also found `opt_error` calls during `opt_loop` (division by zero at lines 747, 753; shift >31 bits at line 1247) that cause longjmp but these are single frees, not double-frees. The double-free requires a malloc failure in `opt_init`.
</EVENT>

--BEGIN AGENT OBSERVATION--
newchunk_nolongjmp(compiler_state_t *cstate, size_t n)
{
        struct block *p;

        p = (struct block *)malloc(n);
        if (p == NULL) {
                /* Could not allocate memory */
                return (NULL);
        }
        p->next = cstate->chunk_head;
        cstate->chunk_head = p;
        cstate->chunk_len += n;
        return ((void *)p);
}

static void *
newchunk(compiler_state_t *cstate, size_t n)
{
        void *p = newchunk_nolongjmp(cstate, n);

        if (p == NULL)
                bpf_error(cstate, "malloc");
        return (p);
}
--END AGENT OBSERVATION--
</EVENT>
